title: instrument-granular-token-credit-meter-and-contextual-error-tags
author: Asha Kapoor
description: Context / motivation: customers and SREs have surfaced incidents where token-cost spikes correlate with rapid retry loops and downstream errors, but our current token-level telemetry and logs make it hard to attribute cost to a causal error surface. This PR introduces two complementary observability features: (1) a Token Credit Meter that tracks per-invocation 'credit' consumption per token phase and exposes rate-normalized delta metrics for short and long tails, and (2) Contextual Error Tags that attach lightweight error-class fingerprints to spans/logs so traces and dashboards can quickly group cost spikes by error mode. Goals: reduce mean time to detect cost-causing errors, enable alert rules that target cost-anomalies with contextual grouping (so noisy long-tail errors don't trigger noisy pages), and provide dashboard panels that let product and SRE teams explore token cost by error cluster. Summary of changes: - Runtime metrics: new counter/gauge set under observations.token_credit.{issued,consumed,expired} with labels: tenant_id, model_name, invocation_stage (prefill, decode, finalize), error_class (optional). Added normalized per-second and per-invocation rate variants. - Trace/log instrumentation: attach contextual_error_tag to spans and emitted logs when downstream adapters return specific error classes (timeout, rate-limit, invalid-response, precondition-failure). The tags are short stable symbols (e.g. err:RT, err:RL) to control cardinality. - Aggregation and rollups: Introduced a lightweight aggregator that produces hourly rollups for token credit deltas and attaches representative error_class and top-k prompt hashes. - Dashboards: new Token Credit Explorer dashboard with three panels: credit-slope (rate-normalized delta), error-cluster heatmap (token-cost by error_class and stage), and representative-invocation inspector (links to trace viewer and sampled logs). - Alerts and tuning: new composite alert templates: TokenCreditSpikeHigh (S1) hooks to credit-slope p99 > threshold for >5m with error_class weight. Added quiet window support and alert dampeners that use error_class frequency to reduce noise. - Backwards compatibility: all new metrics are additive and follow naming conventions; tagging is optional and defaults to empty string when not present. Migration plan: - Rollout as a staged deploy: first enable runtime metric emission in canary (10% traffic), enable trace tagging in debug mode (1% sampled traces) for two days, then scale to 100% and enable hourly rollups. - Dashboard published to shared Observability folder and linked in the SRE runbook. Checklist: - [x] Metric names and units documented in metrics reference - [x] Dashboard panels reviewed by observability team - [x] Alert thresholds proposed and validated against 30d historical data - [x] Performance microbench added to ensure instrumentation adds <1% p99 latency overhead - [x] Owner and escalation documented (SRE/Observability) Related work: this ties into ENG-10294 (token attribution refactor) and ENG-10310 (alert noise reduction). A support ticket SUP-887 reported customer-facing cost regressions that motivated the work. Links: dashboard: https://grafana.internal/redwood/d/token-credit-explorer, runbook: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-10294/runbook, historical-queries: https://analytics.internal/query/credit-deltas.

review_comments: Miguel Torres: Nice end-to-end design. A couple of thoughts: (1) error_class cardinality — can we cap to a curated set and fall back to 'other' to avoid explosion? (2) For the rollups, prefer retaining only top-5 prompt hashes to avoid PII risk.
Asha Kapoor: Agree on both points. The implementation uses a curated enum for error_class and rollups store only top-5 prompt hash prefixes (sha256:8) and are redacted per data-retention policy.
Lena Fischer: CI initially failed in perf runs (microbench showed 1.7% p99 overhead). Suggest switching tag emission behind a sampling flag and optimize hot-path logging to reduce allocation.
Asha Kapoor: Addressed — added sampling flag in runtime (default off during canary) and switched to zero-allocation tag path; microbench re-run shows 0.6% p99 overhead.
Samir Patel: Approving pending a short blurb in the SRE runbook about how to tune quiet-window thresholds for teams with bursty traffic.
Asha Kapoor: Runbook updated with tuning guidelines and example thresholds per tenant tier.
release_notes: Added Token Credit Meter (token_credit.* metrics), contextual_error_tag for spans/logs, Token Credit Explorer dashboard, and alert templates for token-cost spike detection. Rollout is staged; follow SRE runbook for tuning.
notes_for_oncall: If TokenCreditSpikeHigh fires, check token_credit.consumed p99 and error_class distribution. Use representative invocation links in dashboard to jump to trace. Quiet-window and error_class dampening are applied; escalate to Observability if noisy alerts persist.
